versions.changelog: v1.7.6: Added 'Working out the actual deadline' section (calendar-day counting, s.50(a), ad-hoc holidays, points to construction-law SOP calculator). Replaced Companion skill section with 4-step end-to-end workflow. Wizard prompt sharpened to nudge toward specific dates. No cross-skill code coupling — paired via documentation only.
v1.7.5: Sanitised test docstrings/comments — removed function-call patterns in English text that ClawHub static analysis was pattern-matching as suspicious.dynamic_code_execution.
v1.7.4: Replaced string-grep forbidden-imports test with ast.parse tree-walking — catches compile/exec/eval regardless of whitespace or indirection, no false-positives on comments/docstrings/strings.

v1.7.3: Rewrote test_smoke.py to eliminate ClawScan suspicious.dynamic_code_execution flag — tests now import main() directly via unittest.mock.patch instead of subprocess. Tightened forbidden-imports list (urllib.request/error not blanket urllib; added importlib, pickle, marshal, compile). Tests run 20x faster.

v1.7.2: Required-key validation (6 mandatory keys for --file mode), unified _safe_write helper, interactive mode error handling, docs: --help output, no telemetry, files written, required keys table, unittest over pytest
v1.7.1: Added forbidden-imports test (enforces no-network/no-subprocess security claim); updated Python requirement from 3.6+ to 3.10+ (honest about what's actually tested)

v1.7.0: Replaced example scenario with realistic PSSCOC EOT case (Contractor responding to SO rejection under Clause 13.2). Updated strategy_input.json with correct flat-key schema, regenerated strategy_report_sample.md from actual script output, improved test docstrings. Includes v1.6.1 changes: JSON input validation, file I/O error handling, dead code removal.
v1.6.1: JSON input validation (dict check, unknown key warnings), file I/O error handling (friendly messages for missing/unreadable files), removed dead code (_prompt_yesno)
Added examples (PSSCOC 2014), smoke tests, LICENSE, vocabulary normalisation, removed bespoke wording, clarified references framing

Added comprehensive Delay Analysis Study Guide — SCL Protocol 22 Core Principles, 7 delay analysis methods (incl. Retrospective Longest Path), negative float and EOT entitlement, concurrent delay (Malmaison/North Midland/City Inn), pacing delays, disruption causation (Walter Lilly test), force majeure vs hardship, COVID-19 lessons, 15 key cases with citations, full definitions glossary. Total: 22 reference documents.

Major expansion: Integrated full Construction Claim Strategy Practical Tools Guide v1.4. Added 11 new reference documents — Notice Requirements Checklist, Expert Engagement, Legal Precedents, Concurrent Delay Strategy, Disruption Claims Strategy, Delay Analysis Methods, Arbitration Tactics & Prolongation Strategies, ADR Overview, Quantum Worked Examples (8 examples: Eichleay/Hudson/Emden/Measured Mile/Actual Cost/Total Cost), Common Pitfalls, Risk Assessment Framework, Record Keeping Checklist, Claim Preparation Checklist. Total: 21 reference documents.

Major content expansion: 7-dimension detailed guide with good/bad examples, 4 fully worked examples (Variation, EOT, Disruption, Combined EOT+Disruption) with complete strategy worksheets and sample response letters, blank strategy worksheet template, EOT vs Disruption comparison table. All fully generic with proper disclaimers.

Major content update: detailed argument ranking guide with response structures, primary+fallback combination patterns, argument-disclosure interaction table, response letter template, quick reference card, training workshop guide. All fully generic. Added 4 new reference documents.
Fully sanitized — all generic/neutral language. No jurisdiction-specific references. Improved wizard with validation. Legal disclaimer added.
Scrubbed all project-specific references. All examples now generic/hypothetical. Added disclaimer.

Initial release — strategic planning framework for construction claim responses. Covers situation assessment, scope control, direction decisions, argument ranking, disclosure control, response architecture, and risk assessment.
